item.text: {"verdict":"needs-attention","summary":"The commit adds a statusline sidecar writer, but the implementation can block or fail in common Windows/Git-Bash environments and can break the statusline path if optional tooling is missing.","findings":[{"severity":"high","title":"Statusline can fail completely when the configured Python is unavailable","body":"The script runs with `set -u` but not `-e`, then unconditionally executes `$PYTHON_BIN` in the `if ! ...` branch and again in the error logger. If the hard-coded default `Z:/venvs/claude/Scripts/python.exe` is absent or not executable, the sidecar step returns 127, the fallback logger also fails, and the script continues to `printf ... | \"${STATUSLINE_CMD[@]}\"`. That leaves a noisy failed hook path and no sidecar state. For a statusline hook, optional sidecar capture should degrade silently when Python is unavailable, or resolve Python from the active environment before use.","file":".claude/hooks/scripts/context_window_statusline.sh","line_start":12,"line_end":95,"confidence":0.86,"recommendation":"Guard with `command -v`/`[ -x ]` before invoking Python, or use the same interpreter/runtime already guaranteed by the hook environment. If unavailable, skip only the sidecar write and still run the base statusline cleanly."},{"severity":"medium","title":"Concurrent statusline invocations can lose sidecar updates","body":"The read-modify-write sequence reads the whole sidecar JSON, updates one `session_id`, writes a temp file, then replaces the original without any lock. Statusline commands may run frequently and multiple Claude sessions can invoke this script at the same time. Two processes that read the same old file can each write a valid replacement, but the later replace drops the earlier session update.","file":".claude/hooks/scripts/context_window_statusline.sh","line_start":54,"line_end":75,"confidence":0.82,"recommendation":"Add an interprocess lock around the sidecar read/update/replace operation, or write per-session files and aggregate them elsewhere."},{"severity":"medium","title":"Corrupt sidecar JSON makes updates permanently stop without diagnostics","body":"Only `OSError` is caught around the sidecar read/write block. If `context_window_sidecar.json` exists but contains partial or invalid JSON, `json.load(f)` raises `JSONDecodeError`, the Python process exits non-zero, and the outer logger records only a generic subprocess failure. The invalid file remains in place, so future invocations keep failing instead of recovering.","file":".claude/hooks/scripts/context_window_statusline.sh","line_start":56,"line_end":80,"confidence":0.8,"recommendation":"Catch `json.JSONDecodeError` and either reset to `{}` with an explicit `sidecar_read` error log entry or move the bad file aside before rewriting."}],"next_steps":["Make the sidecar writer best-effort when Python or ccstatusline dependencies are unavailable.","Protect the sidecar update with locking or per-session files.","Handle invalid existing sidecar JSON explicitly."]}
